short: Doubled the size of the country with a purchase he doubted he had the power to make.
full:
Jefferson's inauguration in 1801 followed an electoral tie with Aaron Burr that took thirty-six ballots in the House to resolve. He cut the army, repealed internal taxes, and set about reducing the federal debt, treating the election as a restoration of republican simplicity.

In 1803 Napoleon offered the whole of Louisiana for roughly fifteen million dollars. Jefferson, a strict constructionist who doubted the Constitution permitted it, bought it anyway, adding some 828,000 square miles and sending Lewis and Clark to survey the ground. Marbury v. Madison, decided the same year by his cousin and adversary John Marshall, established judicial review. His second term went badly: the Embargo Act of 1807, intended to coerce Britain and France by withholding American trade, wrecked New England shipping, was widely evaded, and was repealed days before he left office.
